OT: Cache contextual input classes and RuleSet digests (#6233)

Extend the chained-context external cache with a mapping cache for
input classes, and summarize the first input classes of each format-2
contextual RuleSet in a per-RuleSet digest word built when the cache
is created.  The digest lets the apply path skip a RuleSet walk when
the next input glyph cannot match any rule's first class; collisions
only cause the normal rule walk, and allocation failure falls back to
the uncached path.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Code <noreply@anthropic.com>

OT: Cache contextual lookahead classes (#6234)

Extend the chained-context external cache with a mapping cache for
lookahead classes, sharing it with backtrack matching when the two
ClassDefs are the same object.  Class lookups along the lookahead
sequence dominate chained-context matching cost on cacheable fonts.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Code <noreply@anthropic.com>

coupling: Heap-buffer-overflow in OT::ChainContextFormat2_5::external_cache_create (src/hb-ot-layout-gsubgpos.hh), delocalized across the two contextual-cache commits. Commit A (#6233) converts the chained-context external cache into a variable-length allocation (binary coverage cache + one class mapping cache + a per-RuleSet digest array) and hand-computes the byte size as sizeof(hb_ot_layout_binary_cache_t) + sizeof(hb_ot_layout_mapping_cache_t) + count*sizeof(hb_ot_layout_ruleset_digest_t) -- exactly matching the cache layout that A itself creates, so A alone is correct (verified: probe runs clean on the tree containing only A). Commit B (#6234) then extends the same external_cache_t with a second mapping cache (lookahead_class), clears it in external_cache_create, and uses it for lookahead/backtrack class matching, without touching A's size expression. With both applied, the allocation is 512 bytes (sizeof(hb_ot_layout_mapping_cache_t)) short of the struct it initializes: clearing lookahead_class writes a 512-byte hb_cache_t at offset 768 into a 776+8n-byte heap block, and the per-RuleSet digest fill writes even further. Reached from the public API by hb_shape on any font whose GSUB or GPOS contains a format-2 chained-context lookup referenced by an enabled feature, via the lookup accelerator's external_cache_create. Neither commit is faulty in isolation: A's size expression matches A's struct exactly, and B's member addition is correct under every allocation scheme that accounts for the whole struct -- including the sizeof(external_cache_t)-based malloc that preceded A. B's diff never even shows the size expression (it sits outside the hunk context of B's clear() addition), so a commit-by-commit reviewer sees two locally-correct diffs. A correct repair is non-local: it must make A's size expression cover the member B added (or otherwise re-derive the size from the final struct), which requires holding both commits' invariants at once; fixing either single diff in isolation either reverts that commit's feature or leaves the under-allocation in place.
